### Thinking about the problem

We want to know how many months, $t$, it will take before the area of the meadow, $A$, decreases to $500$ hectares.
  
So we need to find the value of $t$ for which $A=500$. 

Substituting $500$ in for $A$ in the model gives us the following equation.

$500=1562.5\cdot 10\^{{-0.1t}}$

### Solving the equation

We can solve the equation as shown below.  

$\begin{align}1562.5\cdot 10\^{{-0.1t}}&=500\\\\
10\^{{-{0.1t}}}&=0.32\\\\
-0.1t&=\log\left(0.32\right)\\\\
t&=-10\log\left(0.32\right)\\\\
\end{align}$

It will take $-10\log\left(0.32\right)$ months for the area of the meadow to decrease to $500$ hectares.  

The expression above represents an *exact* solution to the equation.  We can use a calculator to approximate the value of the expression, but this will be a rounded *inexact* answer.

question.content:
A large open meadow near your city is shrinking in size because developers have started building new homes there.  

The relationship between $A$, the area of the meadow, in hectares, and $t$, the elapsed time, in months, since the construction began is modeled by the following function.

$A=1562.5\cdot 10\^{-0.1t}$

**How many months of construction will there be before the area of the meadow decreases to $500$ hectares?**  
*Give an exact answer expressed as a base-$10$ logarithm.*

 [[☃ expression 1]] months
